verses.text: But know this, that in the last days, grievous times will come.
For men will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
without natural affection, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, fierce, not lovers of good,
traitors, headstrong, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God;
holding a form of godliness, but having denied its power. Turn away from these, also.
For some of these are people who creep into houses, and take captive gullible women loaded down with sins, led away by various lusts,
always learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
Even as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so do these also oppose the truth; men corrupted in mind, who concerning the faith, are rejected.
But they will proceed no further. For their folly will be evident to all men, as theirs also came to be.
But you did follow my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, steadfastness,
persecutions, and sufferings: those things that happened to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I endured those persecutions. The Lord delivered me out of them all.
Yes, and all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution.
But evil men and impostors will grow worse and worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But you remain in the things which you have learned and have been assured of, knowing from whom you have learned them.
From infancy, you have known the holy Scriptures which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith, which is in Christ Jesus.
Every Scripture is God-breathed and  profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.

footnotes.content: Paul warns Timothy plainly: hard times are coming. We don't know the day or hour, but the heart that clings to Jesus need not fear. When the world grows cruel, His mercy only grows closer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Self-love. Money-love. Pride without truth. I've watched people hollow themselves out chasing these. But a heart turned toward Jesus grows generous and humble without meaning to—it's just what happens when we stop serving ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Without natural affection. Unforgiving. Fierce. I notice how bitterness closes people off from love, even from their own kin. The Gospel cracks that hard heart open—it teaches us to forgive as we've been forgiven, to feel again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God. I've seen both kinds of pleasure—one empties you, one fills. The second kind only comes when you've made peace with the One who matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A form of godliness without power. These are the hollow ones—all the words, no transformation. Paul tells Timothy to turn away. That's mercy, not cruelty: better to walk with the true thing than to waste your years on a counterfeit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Creeping into houses, taking captive gullible women. These false teachers target the weary and troubled—those carrying heavy shame. It's why we need friends who know Jesus to help us see the truth when deceivers come near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Always learning, never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Some spend their whole lives reading about God without ever meeting Him. The truth isn't an idea to collect—it's a Person to know, and that changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses—by tradition, Pharaoh's magicians who mimicked God's signs but had no real power. These false teachers do the same: they look impressive, but they have no standing before the Lord. In the end, He's the only one who matters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their folly will be evident to all men. Falsehood has no roots. It blooms fast, loud, and impressive—but truth outlasts it every time. We can trust that.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, steadfastness. Paul reminds Timothy: you know what a true believer looks like in the dailiness of it. Character in action—that's the proof that speaks louder than any argument.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those things at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra—Paul names the real places where he suffered for the Gospel (Acts 13-14). He didn't shrink from it. He endured because the Lord was with him. When we stumble into our own hard moments, we can trust He's faithful then too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution. This isn't doom—it's honesty. The world resists what it doesn't control. But Jesus walks with us through it, and His company is worth the cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Evil men and impostors will grow worse and worse, deceiving and being deceived. That's a cycle—they fool themselves first, then they fool others. It's a mercy when we see it coming and step back toward the truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Remain in the things you have learned and been assured of. Paul calls Timothy to hold fast, not because change is evil, but because truth is worth holding. When you know the hand of the one who taught you was guiding you toward Jesus, you can stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From infancy, you have known the holy Scriptures. Timothy learned Scripture as a child (his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois taught him, as 2 Timothy 1:5 tells us). Early roots in God's Word set a course for a lifetime. What a gift to give a child.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every Scripture is God-breathed. The very breath of the Almighty formed these words—for teaching, reproof, correction, instruction in righteousness. When we open these pages, we're not just reading ancient texts; we're listening to God speak to us, here and now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: That the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work. Readers today hear an echo of this in their own lives: when we stay in Scripture and let it shape us, the Spirit makes us ready for whatever He calls us to. As of 2026-10, I'm still amazed at how often He brings just the right word at just the right moment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
